content: The columns `traffic_loader.sample_corridor` emits, minus `local_weekday`, which the loader gained after the committed series was collected and which is derivable from `sampled_at`. Extra columns are allowed: the series carries the `year`/`month`/`day`/`hour` partition keys from the raw zone.

One sample is one row per trunk corridor, and 14 corridors pass the `CORRIDOR_MAX_MEAN_HOP_KM` gate (18 match `TRUNK_ROUTE_PATTERN`). `sample_corridors` logs and skips a corridor whose Mapbox call fails, so a short sample is written without any error upstream; this is where it gets noticed.

Same guard for a multi-sample batch, where the row count alone cannot tell a missing corridor from a missing hour. If OSM edits change which corridors survive the hop filter, change this number deliberately.
OSM relation id of the corridor, stored as a string; `fct_corridor_travel_time` joins it to `dim_routes`.

Mirrors `TRUNK_ROUTE_PATTERN` in ingestion/constants.py. Only the trunk BRT systems are sampled; a feeder route here means the corridor selection regressed and is spending Mapbox quota on the wrong thing.
ISO-8601 in UTC, still a string in the raw zone. The staging model derives Quito time (UTC-5, no DST) from it.
The grain: one row per corridor per sample. A duplicate would double-count a corridor in every peak-hour aggregate.
At least two points to route between; at most `MAPBOX_MAX_WAYPOINTS` (25), the hard API limit the loader downsamples to.

Re-asserts the loader's own scrambling gate, `CORRIDOR_MAX_MEAN_HOP_KM = 1.0`: a corridor whose OSM stop order is not geographic would be routed as a zigzag and must never reach this table. Healthy corridors sit at 0.53-0.81 km.

The payload of the whole dataset. Strictly positive: zero or negative is not a slow corridor, it is a broken response, and a zero would also have produced a null `mean_speed_kmh`. The ceiling of four hours is far above the observed 855-5,341 s, on corridors of 8-31 km; anything longer is not a traversal.

Plausibility bounds for a BRT corridor, not a reroute detector. Mapbox reroutes between calls even with fixed waypoints (up to ~20% spread per corridor in the committed series, data/samples/README.md), and that is a documented property of the source that the analysis accounts for, not a row that fails validation. Telling a 5% reroute from a 50% one needs the corridor's own history, which belongs in the warehouse, not in a single-batch gate. These bounds catch the gross case: a response that routed somewhere else entirely.
The loader writes null here only when `duration_seconds` is zero, so this is a second witness to the same failure.
An urban bus corridor does not average above 80 km/h, and below 5 km/h the duration or distance unit is wrong. Observed 18-40 km/h.

Zero segments means the `congestion` annotation was missing from the response, in which case the loader writes `congestion_known_pct = 0.0` and every coverage column is meaningless rather than merely low.
`segments_known` is `segments_total` minus the `unknown` count, so it can never exceed the total.
No lower bound beyond zero on purpose: coverage is structured by time of day (1.8% at 04:00 local against 56.5% at 21:00), so a low value is a real observation, not a defect.

meta.description: Expectations for the raw Mapbox corridor travel-time series (corridor_travel_time_series.parquet). Validates presence of the columns traffic_loader emits, the (route_id, sampled_at) grain, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, a full set of trunk corridors per batch (guards against corridors the loader skipped after a failed Mapbox call), the loader's own waypoint and stop-spacing limits, strictly positive durations, and plausibility ranges on distance, speed and congestion coverage.

content: Validated by `raw_samples_checkpoint` against `data/samples/traffic/corridor_travel_time_series.parquet`. The single-snapshot `corridor_travel_time.parquet` is not validated: with one `sampled_at` it cannot exercise the series-level checks, and the samples README marks the series as the file to build on.
